sub_questions.question: Why does it say I'm out of credits when I haven't used the app much?
Can you fix this (restore the ability to use the app)?

claims.claim: The credit allowance is different depending on the workspace's plan.
claims.guide_evidence: Sandbox | Free | 200 credits, one-time (does not renew) ... Professional ... 5,000 credits/month ... Team ... 10,000 credits/month

claims.claim: On the free Sandbox plan, the 200 message credits are a one-time allowance that does not renew.
On Sandbox, even light use can exhaust the credits.
claims.guide_evidence: larger or multimodal models ... around 10 credits per response. A workspace that mostly uses a heavier model will exhaust its credit balance noticeably faster

claims.claim: On Professional or Team, credits reset monthly.
claims.guide_evidence: waits for the next monthly credit reset (paid plans)

claims.claim: On a paid plan, running out of credits mid-cycle almost always means a billing sync delay on Dify's side.
That billing sync delay corrects itself automatically, so no action is needed.
claims.guide_evidence: Once a workspace's credits are used up, model calls on Dify-hosted credits stop working until the workspace either connects its own API key for that provider or waits for the next monthly credit reset

claims.claim: The customer can check the Billing page to see their plan and remaining credits.
claims.guide_evidence: Only the workspace owner and admins can open the Billing page and manage a subscription.

claims.claim: The customer's options are connecting their own provider key or upgrading.
claims.guide_evidence: To move beyond the included credits ... a workspace connects its own model provider

evaluation.rationale: The answer makes up a cause, claiming that paid-plan users who run out mid-cycle are almost always seeing a "billing sync delay" that fixes itself with "no action needed". The guide says nothing like this. It says model calls stop until the workspace connects its own key or the monthly reset arrives, so the customer may wait for a fix that won't come. The answer also skips the explanation the guide does give: credits are charged per model, and heavier models use up to 10 credits per response. It also directs the customer to the Billing page without noting that only owners and admins can open it.
